thread:
maria: Hey team, Lantern hit sustained burst traffic starting 09:12 UTC and their Dedicated pool exhausted burst credits. Customers seeing 429s and elevated p95 latency. Can we triage?
aj: I see alerts — admission_controller.rejections spiked at 09:13, burst_credits.balance_for_pool=0.0. What was the traffic pattern?
maria: Traffic went from ~220 tps to ~1.2k tps over 2 minutes. They have a small dedicated pool (4xA100 equiv).
devin: Do we have proxy logs for the failed requests? Any auth failures or just admission rejections?
maria: Mostly admission rejections (429). A handful of timeouts from backend (504) around 09:18. No auth errors in quick scan.
sophie: Opening pool telemetry — autoscale didn't add nodes until ~09:16. Autoscaler backlog climbed then eventually spawned an extra instance at 09:17 but too late. Looks like prewarm=off for this customer.
chris: Can someone paste the admission_controller config for Lantern's account? Interested in headroom, burst window and credit config.
aj: Config snapshot from vault:
```
account: lantern
dedicated_pool_id: dp-87
admission_controller:
  tps_slo: 300
  burst_window_seconds: 60
  burst_credit_capacity: 18000  # tokens
  headroom_fraction: 0.2
  min_reserved_slots: 2
```
Note: their tps_slo is 300 but observed sustained >1k.
devin: Burst_credit_capacity is tokens not requests — Lantern uses long responses avg 45 tokens per request so 18000 tokens ~= 400 requests. Burst window 60s, so bursts over that burn credits fast.
maria: Customer says their workload is mostly short chat turns but spiky from campaign. They expected Dedicated to absorb short spikes.
sophie: Investigating noisy neighbor: there was a cross-customer job on same host at 09:10 doing long decode loops (customer: Borealis) — high GPU mem and slow kernel scheduling. Host metrics show NVLink saturation and higher GPU kernel queuing. Could have delayed autoscale signals.
ach-ops-bot: Deploy notice: cluster-autoscaler scaled pool dp-87 by +1 at 09:17 (reason: queue_length>40).
aj: Immediate mitigations we can do: 1) temporarily increase Lantern's burst_credit_capacity; 2) enable prewarm to add warm instances; 3) route a percentage of Lantern traffic to fallback hosted model/region; 4) kill/migrate noisy neighbor job. Which do we want now?
maria: Customer asked for fastest fix without reboots: increase burst credits and enable a fast prewarm. Can we bump credits while we plan longer-term?
devin: I can patch admission config with a +50% credit bump (to 27000 tokens) and set prewarm=true with target_warm=1. That should reduce rejections within 30s of config rollout. Note: this increases cost.
sophie: I'll start migration plan for the noisy neighbor job — contacting infra to drain the problematic host.
ach-ops-bot: Action executed: admission_config.patch applied by devin at 09:23. New burst_credit_capacity=27000, prewarm=enabled.
maria: Customer reports reduction in 429s at 09:25, but p95 still elevated.
devin: p95 spike likely due to KV-cache miss and restarted kernels during scale. Suggest they temporary lower model size or route heavy requests to a hosted smaller model.
chris: Repro steps we should capture for postmortem: 1) run a synthetic ramp (curl in a loop) to replicate burst: 120 -> 1200 tps over 90s; 2) verify admission credit burn math using avg tokens=45; 3) observe autoscale lag on pool with and without noisy neighbor.
maria: I'll share a short repro script for support to run:
```
# approximate repro (uses internal loadgen)
for i in {1..1200}; do
  loadgen --target dp-87 --rate $i --duration 60 --payload "short chat"
done
```
Note: internal loadgen will run with token_estimate=45.
aj: Logged an incident ticket: INC-2026-0421. Assigning to eng-runtime and infra.
sophie: Also recommend we adjust headroom_fraction for small pools. With headroom_fraction 0.2 on a 4-node pool that gives us low effective admission slack. Proposal: add policy to set headroom fraction = max(0.2, 0.5 for pools <=4). I'll draft RFC.
devin: For immediate SLA protection we can add an automated fallback rule: if burst_credit_balance < 10% route 30% traffic to hosted fallback model with same prompt semantics. Would keep user experience and reduce overall burn. Need product signoff though.
maria: Customer wants a post-incident summary and cost impact estimate for credit bump + prewarm. I'll collect numbers.
ach-ops-bot: Monitoring rule created: alert if admission_rejections > 10/min for >3min on any dedicated pool.
chris: Next steps: (1) Sophie to migrate noisy neighbor job off host (in progress); (2) Devin to open PR for autoscaler tuning and fallback routing prototype; (3) Maria to coordinate customer comms + cost estimate; (4) Aj to update incident ticket with logs and config snapshots.
sophie: Host drain started 09:40, will report when eviction complete.
devin: PR opened: github.com/redwood/eng-runtime/pull/4122 — autoscaler tuning and headroom policy.
aj: Added attachments to INC-2026-0421: proxy logs, admission metrics CSV, host telemetry.
maria: Customer emailed back: "Thanks — 429s dropped ~90%, still seeing occasional slow responses. We'll accept fallback route for next 2 hours"
chris: Good. For the postmortem include: math of token->request conversion, autoscale median lag for this pool (3.5min), noisy neighbor kernel preemption evidence, and recommendation checklist (prewarm=true for predictable bursts, conservative headroom for small pools, automated fallback rules).
maria: I'll draft the postmortem and share in #postmortems. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
